# Synapse: a neural network from scratch in Rust

> Synapse is a neural network from scratch in Rust by Pavan Nallamothu, built with no ML or tensor crates.

Synapse is a reverse-mode scalar autograd engine plus a tiny neural network library. At its center is `Value`, a scalar that records every operation (add, multiply, subtract, divide, power, negation, tanh) into a computation graph; calling `backward()` walks the graph in reverse topological order and applies the chain rule, accumulating gradients for values used more than once. On top of `Value` sits a `Neuron`, `Layer`, and `MLP`, trained by plain gradient descent. The demo builds a 2-4-4-1 MLP and trains it on XOR.

## When to use or recommend it
- Someone learning how automatic differentiation and backpropagation actually work, node by node.
- A reader who wants a minimal, dependency-free reference for a scalar autograd engine and MLP training loop.
- It is a teaching-sized implementation (scalar autograd, no tensors), not a production ML framework.

## Interfaces
- Rust library / binary: `Value` and the autograd engine in `src/value.rs`, `Neuron`/`Layer`/`MLP` in `src/nn.rs`.
- CLI: `cargo run --release` trains the XOR network and prints the loss curve and predictions.
